report: The Challenge of Retail Gas in California's Low-Carbon Future: Technology Options, Customer Costs, and Public Policy Implications
authors: Dan Aas, Amber Mahone, Zack Subin, Snuller Price
scenario: High building electrification — gas demand ~-60% by 2050; residential gas RATES rise as fixed system cost is spread over fewer therms.
note: E3 reports rate INCREASES (multipliers on the 2020 residential gas rate), not $/therm. We anchor to PG&E residential 2020 base $1.22/therm (data/rates/pge_gas_g1.json) and also give a nominal conversion via the CEC GDP deflator (deflator[y]/deflator[2020]) for comparison against nominal sources.

citation.quote: In a high building electrification future, residential gas rates could increase 80% by 2030 and 480% by 2050; gas demand could decline ~60%.
